title: Chapter 18 — Built-In and Integrated Refrigeration
intro: Built-in vs. integrated vs. columns, the engineering deltas, and panel-ready craft.

sections.title: Three Tiers of Integration
sections.content:
Built-in: shallower depth than freestanding, sits flush with cabinetry, finished sides. Integrated: designed to accept custom panels that match the cabinetry, nearly invisible. Column: separate full-size refrigerator and freezer units that can be placed anywhere in the kitchen.

Each tier serves a different customer and a different kitchen design. Know the differences because the customer — and especially their designer — will ask.

sections.title: Panel-Ready Requirements
sections.content:
Panel-ready units require custom panels built by the cabinetmaker. That means lead time, measurements, and coordination between you, the designer, and the cabinet shop.

If you sell a panel-ready unit without confirming that the cabinetmaker is prepared, you create a delivery that sits in the kitchen unfinished. Coordinate before you close.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating built-in and integrated knowledge, ask:

Can the salesperson explain the differences between built-in, integrated, and column units?
Do they coordinate panel-ready orders with the cabinetmaker and designer?
Do they understand the lead time and measurement requirements?
